description: Curated deity iconography for image prompts and captions (core/iconography.py). Only well-established attributes from the standard references listed under 'sources' are recorded. A field that the references do not settle is null (never guessed); lineage variants are recorded as separate forms or in 'notes'. Sources are cited at the level of the work, not the page.

buddha_families.description: The five Buddha families (pancakula) of tantric Buddhism with the correspondences standard in Tibetan sources: the presiding Buddha (lord), his direction in the mandala, the element, the wisdom, the afflictive emotion (poison) that wisdom transforms, and the family emblem. A deity's 'buddha_family' names its family only where the references settle it, and is null otherwise.
buddha_families.variant_note: This is the common arrangement (the Vajradhatu mandala; the peaceful Buddhas of the Bardo Thodol). In some tantras, notably the Guhyasamaja, Akshobhya presides at the centre and Vairocana sits in the east, and the Bardo Thodol gives Vairocana a blue body and Vajrasattva-Akshobhya a white one; the correspondences of the two families move with them. Lists of elements and poisons also vary between texts. Seed syllables follow the common Tibetan set (OṂ, HŪṂ, TRAṂ, HRĪḤ, ĀḤ) and move with their Buddhas where Vairocana and Akshobhya trade places. Japanese Shingon uses other seeds: VAṂ for Mahāvairocana in the Vajradhātu mandala (A in the Garbhadhātu), HŪṂ, TRĀḤ, HRĪḤ and AḤ.

forms.label: Shakyamuni Buddha touching the earth
forms.posture: seated in the full lotus (vajra) posture

hands.position: reaching down over the right knee
hands.mudra: the earth-touching gesture (bhumisparsha mudra), fingertips touching the ground
the meditation gesture (dhyana mudra)

forms.features: the crown protuberance (ushnisha), the curl between the brows (urna) and elongated earlobes
forms.halo: a round halo behind the head and an aureole of light around the body
forms.notes: The throne is frequently a lion throne beneath the lotus; the moon disc is the usual Tibetan seat and is kept here.

deities.individual_iconography_note: The 88 Buddhas of the Chinese repentance liturgy (the 53 Buddhas of the past and the 35 Confession Buddhas) are invoked by name; the liturgy gives them no individual bodily iconography, so no per-Buddha colour, mudra or attribute is recorded. The element, chakra and quality fields in knowledge/eighty_eight_buddhas.json are this app's correspondences, not iconography. (Tibetan art does depict the 35 Confession Buddhas individually, after a visionary system attributed to Tsongkhapa; that set is not curated here.) Images use the generic Buddha form below.

forms.label: a Buddha in meditation
forms.posture: seated in meditation in the full lotus (vajra) posture

hands.mudra: the meditation gesture (dhyana mudra)

forms.features: the crown protuberance (ushnisha), the curl between the brows (urna) and elongated earlobes
forms.halo: a round halo behind the head and an aureole of light around the body
forms.notes: A generic depiction: the golden colour and the marks are the common marks of any Buddha; the meditation gesture is a neutral choice, not an attribute of any particular Buddha.

forms.label: Four-armed Avalokiteshvara (Chenrezig)
forms.posture: seated in the full lotus (vajra) posture
forms.seat: a moon disc on a lotus

hands.mudra: the gesture of joined palms (anjali mudra)

hands.holds: the stem of a white lotus blossoming beside the shoulder

forms.features: an antelope skin draped over the left shoulder
forms.halo: a round halo behind the head and an aureole of light around the body
forms.notes: The most widely depicted Tibetan form of Chenrezig, the deity of the six-syllable mantra.

forms.label: Eleven-faced, thousand-armed Avalokiteshvara
forms.seat: a moon disc on a lotus

hands.mudra: the gesture of joined palms (anjali mudra)
the boon-granting gesture (varada mudra)

forms.other_hands: the remaining arms spread behind in a circular aureole, an eye in the palm of each hand
forms.features: the faces stacked in tiers, peaceful faces below, a wrathful dark face near the top and the red face of Amitabha Buddha at the summit
forms.halo: the circle of a thousand arms forms the aureole
forms.notes: Tibetan form after the Gelongma Palmo (Bhikshuni Lakshmi) lineage: eight principal arms. The colours of the individual faces in the tiers differ between lineages and are left out (null). The East Asian thousand-armed Guanyin, with forty-two principal hands and a different list of implements, is not curated here; the repo's practice text mixes elements of both.

deities.notes: The avalokiteshvara practice visualises the thousand-armed form; the default form for images is the four-armed Chenrezig. Of the lotus (padma) family of Amitabha, who is shown at the summit of his head.

forms.label: Green Tara
forms.descriptor: a youthful, gently smiling female deity
forms.posture: seated with the left leg drawn in and the right leg extended, the right foot resting on a small lotus
forms.seat: a moon disc on a lotus

hands.position: resting on the right knee, palm facing outward
hands.mudra: the boon-granting gesture of supreme giving (varada mudra)
the refuge-granting gesture, thumb and ring finger joined and three fingers raised
hands.holds: the stem of a blue utpala lotus blossoming beside the left shoulder

forms.halo: a round halo behind the head and an aureole of light around the body
forms.notes: Many paintings give the right hand a second utpala stem as well. Some texts name the left-hand gesture abhaya (fearlessness) rather than the refuge or three-jewels gesture; the hand shape is the same.

deities.notes: Of the action (karma) family of Amoghasiddhi, whose consort she is in the five-family system.

forms.label: White Tara
forms.posture: seated in the full lotus (vajra) posture
forms.seat: a moon disc on a lotus

hands.position: resting on the right knee, palm facing outward
hands.mudra: the boon-granting gesture of supreme giving (varada mudra)
the refuge-granting gesture, thumb and ring finger joined and three fingers raised
hands.holds: the stem of a white utpala lotus blossoming beside the left shoulder

forms.features: seven eyes: a third eye on the forehead and an eye in each palm and on the sole of each foot
forms.halo: a round halo behind the head and an aureole of light around the body
forms.notes: The utpala often carries three blossoms (bud, half-open, full bloom), and a full moon disc often stands behind her back.

forms.label: Medicine Buddha
forms.posture: seated in the full lotus (vajra) posture

hands.position: resting over the right knee, palm facing outward
hands.mudra: the boon-granting gesture of supreme giving (varada mudra)
hands.holds: a stem of the myrobalan (arura) medicinal plant

hands.mudra: the meditation gesture (dhyana mudra)
hands.holds: an alms bowl filled with medicinal nectar

forms.features: the crown protuberance (ushnisha) and elongated earlobes
forms.halo: a round halo behind the head and an aureole of light around the body
forms.notes: Tibetan form. East Asian images (Yakushi) commonly hold a medicine jar instead; that form is not curated here.

forms.label: Amitabha Buddha
forms.posture: seated in the full lotus (vajra) posture

hands.mudra: the meditation gesture (dhyana mudra)

forms.features: the crown protuberance (ushnisha) and elongated earlobes
forms.halo: a round halo behind the head and an aureole of light around the body
forms.notes: Tibetan form; his throne is traditionally supported by peacocks. Amitayus (crowned, holding a long-life vase) and the standing East Asian welcoming forms are distinct and not curated here.

forms.label: Vajrasattva
forms.posture: seated in the full lotus (vajra) posture
forms.seat: a moon disc on a lotus
forms.halo: a round halo behind the head and an aureole of light around the body
forms.notes: The solitary form. A form in union with a consort is also practised; it is not used for images here.

deities.notes: Of the vajra family of Akshobhya; the Bardo Thodol names him Vajrasattva-Akshobhya.

forms.label: Manjushri with the sword and the book
forms.posture: seated in the full lotus (vajra) posture
forms.seat: a moon disc on a lotus

hands.holds: the stem of a blue utpala lotus that supports a wrapped scripture beside the left shoulder

forms.halo: a round halo behind the head and an aureole of light around the body
forms.notes: The most common Tibetan form; many other forms of Manjushri exist.

forms.label: Four-armed Prajnaparamita
forms.posture: seated in the full lotus (vajra) posture
forms.seat: a moon disc on a lotus

hands.holds: a wrapped palm-leaf scripture of the Perfection of Wisdom

forms.halo: a round halo behind the head and an aureole of light around the body
forms.notes: The gesture of the principal pair of hands differs by lineage (teaching gesture at the heart, or meditation gesture in the lap), so it is left null and not prompted. The heart_sutra practice also offers Avalokiteshvara, the sutra's speaker, as an alternative focus.

forms.label: Eighteen-armed Cundi
forms.posture: seated in the full lotus posture

hands.mudra: the teaching gesture
the gesture of fearlessness (abhaya mudra)

hands.holds: a scripture of the Perfection of Wisdom

forms.features: three eyes, the third on the forehead
forms.notes: The eighteen-armed form of East Asian Buddhism, following the image described in the Cundi Dharani Sutra (Taisho 1076). Published descriptions disagree on which side the fearlessness gesture is on; the list follows the sutra as commonly quoted. The Indian Sadhanamala describes a four-armed form and the Nispannayogavali a twenty-six-armed one (Bhattacharyya); neither is curated here. No Tibetan name is recorded because none is established in the sources consulted.

forms.label: Vairocana Buddha
forms.posture: seated in the full lotus (vajra) posture

hands.mudra: the gesture of turning the wheel of the dharma (dharmachakra mudra)

forms.features: the crown protuberance (ushnisha) and elongated earlobes
forms.halo: a round halo behind the head and an aureole of light around the body
forms.notes: Tibetan form; his throne is traditionally supported by lions. His emblem, the wheel, is shown on the seat or beside him rather than held. The Bardo Thodol gives him a blue body, and the crowned Mahavairocana of the Japanese Vajradhatu mandala makes the wisdom-fist gesture (bodhyagri mudra); neither is curated here. The five Buddhas are also painted crowned and jewelled, in their enjoyment-body (sambhogakaya) aspect, especially in tantric mandalas.

forms.label: Akshobhya Buddha
forms.posture: seated in the full lotus (vajra) posture

hands.position: reaching down over the right knee
hands.mudra: the earth-touching gesture (bhumisparsha mudra), fingertips touching the ground
the meditation gesture (dhyana mudra)

forms.features: the crown protuberance (ushnisha) and elongated earlobes
forms.halo: a round halo behind the head and an aureole of light around the body
forms.notes: Tibetan form; his throne is traditionally supported by elephants. His emblem, the vajra, is held upright in the left hand in some images and stands before him on the seat in others, so no held object is recorded. The Bardo Thodol gives him a white body (as Vajrasattva-Akshobhya), and in the Guhyasamaja he presides at the centre of the mandala. The five Buddhas are also painted crowned and jewelled, in their enjoyment-body (sambhogakaya) aspect, especially in tantric mandalas.

forms.label: Ratnasambhava Buddha
forms.posture: seated in the full lotus (vajra) posture

hands.position: resting over the right knee, palm facing outward
hands.mudra: the boon-granting gesture of supreme giving (varada mudra)
the meditation gesture (dhyana mudra)

forms.features: the crown protuberance (ushnisha) and elongated earlobes
forms.halo: a round halo behind the head and an aureole of light around the body
forms.notes: Tibetan form; his throne is traditionally supported by horses. His emblem, the wish-fulfilling jewel, is held in one hand in some images and set on the seat in others, so no held object is recorded. The five Buddhas are also painted crowned and jewelled, in their enjoyment-body (sambhogakaya) aspect, especially in tantric mandalas.

forms.label: Amoghasiddhi Buddha
forms.posture: seated in the full lotus (vajra) posture

hands.position: raised at the chest, palm facing outward
hands.mudra: the gesture of fearlessness (abhaya mudra)
the meditation gesture (dhyana mudra)

forms.features: the crown protuberance (ushnisha) and elongated earlobes
forms.halo: a round halo behind the head and an aureole of light around the body
forms.notes: Tibetan form; his throne is traditionally supported by garudas (shang-shang). His emblem, the crossed vajra, is held in the left hand in some images and set on the seat in others, so no held object is recorded. The five Buddhas are also painted crowned and jewelled, in their enjoyment-body (sambhogakaya) aspect, especially in tantric mandalas.
